thread:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH — dedicated-pool-routing-anomaly for customer-992 in VPC 'eu2-priv'. Route mismatch probability 0.92. Paging on-call.

incident-bot: Alert details: metric=route_mismatch; pool=dedi-eu-2; sample_count=12; potential_cross_tenant=3. playbook=https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INC/pages/tenant-isolation

sara_ops: picking this up. seeing same alert. pulling logs now.

jonah_oncall: i'm oncall — starting triage. @sara_ops what's the customer impact reported? any evidence of data leakage? :eyes:

tia_se: customer SE (Jenny) DM'd us — they noticed ~3 requests returning responses that looked like another tenant's output (different prompt ids). low volume but contains user-provided text. they have paused traffic on their side.

mike_reliability: ok prioritize isolation. first: identify which containers/pods in dedi-eu-2 have overlapping tenant prefixes. then migrate affected tenant off pool.

enginfra: grabbing pool mapping. command i ran:
```
rdw infra list-pool-mappings --pool dedi-eu-2 --format json | jq '.[] | {tenant, upstream_prefixes}'
```
sample output:
```
{ "tenant": "992", "upstream_prefixes": ["10.20.5.0/24"] }
{ "tenant": "1001", "upstream_prefixes": ["10.20.5.128/25"] }
```
looks like prefix overlap (10.20.5.0/24 vs 10.20.5.128/25). probable cause: a recent autoscale that re-allocated a warm VM with stale route table.

alice_prodsec: if prefixes overlap we have risk of cross-tenant KV/cache hits and potentially returned strings. we need to collect evidence (requests, response payloads, timestamps) and preserve for forensics. do NOT purge logs.

sara_ops: capturing request/response pairs from the last 2 hours. grep + sift on tenant header: `X-Redwood-Tenant: 992` and look for mismatched response tenant ids.

enginfra: pulled binder logs, below is an excerpt where a response for req-id `req-8f3b` shows tenant header mismatch:
```
[2026-03-15T11:07:02Z] req-8f3b tenant=992 routed_to=10.20.5.130 container=nn-infer-7 response_tenant=1001
```
that lines up with the overlap.

jonah_oncall: thanks. mitigation plan: 1) remove tenant 992 from dedi-eu-2 (evict + pin to dedi-eu-3 spare), 2) patch route allocation to avoid overlapping netblocks, 3) rotate any customer keys/token that might have been exposed as precaution.

customer_support: i've informed Jenny (customer SE) that we're investigating and will perform a controlled migration. asked if they want immediate key rotation — they prefer to wait for next update but asked for an incident contact. shared on-call contact.

mike_reliability: i'll run the eviction now using the internal CLI. spacing plan: migrate traffic to dedi-eu-3, keep dedi-eu-2 read-only until we confirm no cross-tenant responses.

jonah_oncall: please paste the exact command you run. want audit trail.

mike_reliability: running:
```
rdw tenant evict --tenant 992 --from-pool dedi-eu-2 --to-pool dedi-eu-3 --reason "routing-prefix-overlap" --dry-run=false
```

deploy-bot: evict job started — job_id=evict-19321-01. logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/evict-19321-01/logs

incident-bot: Action logged: tenant_eviction initiated by mike_reliability.

enginfra: after eviction I validated that 10.20.5.128/25 was deallocated from dedi-eu-2 and assigned to dedi-eu-3. routing table now shows:
```
10.20.5.0/25 -> dedi-eu-2
10.20.5.128/25 -> dedi-eu-3
```
no overlaps detected.

sara_ops: running a quick query for mismatched responses post-eviction window (10m after).

sara_ops: query results: 0 mismatches in the last 10m. sample_count previously impacted=3.

alice_prodsec: collecting copies of the impacted responses (sensitive) and storing in secure evidence bucket with limited access. noted customer id 992, request ids [req-8f3b, req-a12d, req-c44e]. added retention flag and GDPR handling.

customer_support: Jenny confirmed they will rotate API keys on their end as a precaution and will hold on public statements until we provide final impact assessment.

tia_se: recommended customer mitigation: rotate keys, confirm no downstream storage of those 3 responses. offered to join call if needed.

jonah_oncall: next steps/todo: - Create INC ticket and set severity to P2 (potential exposure). - Run full prefix allocation audit for all dedi pools. - Postmortem assigned to enginfra + runtime. - Customer follow-up scheduled in 2 hours.

sara_ops: INC ticket created: INC-2026-992-19321; assigned to enginfra. added timeline and evidence.

mike_reliability: i've also deployed a quick admission-controller check to block overlapping CIDR assignments to pools. patch link: https://git.redwood/infra/pool-cidr-guard/pull/42 — deploying canary now.

deploy-bot: deployment started: canary pool-cidr-guard v0.1.3 -> infra-canary-2. artifact=pool-cidr-guard:0.1.3 sha=abc123

alice_prodsec: recommend we notify legal and compliance. potential PII exposure even if small. also recommend preserving the warm VM used for HD analysis.

enginfra: preserved VM snapshot (dedi-eu-2-130-snap) and attached to evidence ticket.

jonah_oncall: handing off to next on-call (mike_reliability) for follow-up and postmortem. i'll stay reachable.

mike_reliability: taking handoff. will run prefix audit and coordinate postmortem. expected timeline for postmortem draft: 48h.

incident-bot: Pager closed by jonah_oncall. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.

sara_ops: summary for channel: routing-prefix overlap in dedi-eu-2 caused 3 cross-tenant responses for customer-992. tenant evicted and migrated to dedi-eu-3. no additional mismatches observed. evidence preserved, customer notified, postmortem planned.

customer_support: customer acknowledged update and requested an ETA for final report. set to 48h.

jonah_oncall: thanks team. if anything new surfaces ping this thread or escalate. :thumbsup:
